# Solar watts to recharge a 1,000Wh power station

**A 200-watt panel refills it in about 1.5 days of decent sun. For a full recharge in one good day, plan on roughly 300-340W of panels.**

## The formula
Daily energy = panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75. The multiplier covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses. Peak sun hours are the day's sunlight expressed as hours of full-strength sun, not hours of daylight. Most of the US gets about 3-6 per day.

Rearranged: **panel watts = 1,000 ÷ (sun hours × 0.7 to 0.75)**

| Panel size | Energy per day (4.5 sun hrs, 70%) | Time to refill 1,000Wh |
|---|---|---|
| 100W | ~315Wh | ~3 days |
| 200W | ~630Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400W | ~1,260Wh | Under a day |

(Table from [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/); [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station) gets the same 630Wh for a 200W panel.)

## Panel watts for a one-day full recharge
- **6 sun hours:** about 230W
- **5 sun hours:** about 270W ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)), or about 300W with extra station losses counted ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/))
- **4 sun hours:** about 340W
- **3 sun hours:** about 450W
- **Northern winter (about 2 sun hours):** 700W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/))

A simple rule of thumb from [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/): divide the battery's watt-hours by 5. For 1,000Wh, that gives about 200W.

## Check these before buying
1. **Your station's maximum solar input.** If it accepts only 200W, extra panel wattage adds nothing. Mid-range 1,000-1,500Wh units often allow 400-800W, but check your model's spec sheet.
2. **The input voltage window.** Panel open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside it. Panels wired in series add voltage, which can damage the station if it goes over.
3. **Loads while charging.** If you run devices during the day, the net charge is slower.

## A product option
If your station accepts 400W and a 12-60V input, the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is one fit. Its Voc is 45.3V and it comes with MC4-to-XT60 and DC adapters. It is listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (the page says the code expires 2026-12-30). It weighs 18.5kg, which is heavy for a folding panel. The page is an affiliate listing, so the site earns a commission if you buy through it. If your station caps solar input at 200W, a 200W panel is the better match.

If you tell me your station model, I can check its solar input limit and suggest a matching panel.
